title: Developer Ownership
levelNote: The mandatory arbiter sweep was run and came up thin: the developer front-loaded a crisp, specific, well-scoped research request, handed the AI no judgment or decision, and the single low-risk fact-finding task shipped no code and warranted no review or domain due diligence.

reviewNecessity.note: Review/QA/test necessity was never discussed in this session — no code change was made, so no review consideration arose. This is a single-turn research-and-summarize task with no diff to review.

items.title: Crisp, scoped intent front-loaded with explicit acceptance
items.quote: Especially the Task with Haiku model. Summarize the findings.
items.detail: In the sole user turn the developer fully owned the intent: they named the exact capabilities to investigate (whether `claude -p` can use WebSearch and the Task tool), singled out the specific case that mattered to them ("Especially the Task with Haiku model"), and stated the acceptance criterion ("Summarize the findings"). Nothing about the goal, scope, or deliverable was left for the AI to infer or invent — the AI was handed a specified execution task (research these facts and summarize them), which is exactly the delegation the tool is for. This is intent ownership done well, and the emphasis clause shows the developer directing the research rather than outsourcing what to care about.
